I haven't changed anything yet. This folder is the Flask-Admin library's own source code, not your app, and none of your admin views are in here.

The 20 comes from the library default, `page_size: int = 20` in `flask_admin/model/base.py:898`. I could change that line, but then every Flask-Admin view everywhere would load every row with no paging, and a library update would undo it. That's the wrong place for the fix.

The right fix is one line in your own view class. The library already supports turning paging off: setting `page_size = 0` loads all rows and hides the pager (`flask_admin/model/base.py:2262`).

```python
class MyModelView(ModelView):
    page_size = 0  # show all rows on one page
```

Put it on the view for that list page, or on a shared base class if you want it on every list. One catch: with thousands of rows the page will load slowly, because everything renders at once. If that becomes a problem, there's a middle option. Set `can_set_page_size = True`, `page_size_options = (20, 50, 100, 1000)` and `page_size = 1000` (the default has to be one of the options), and you also get a page-size dropdown.

Tell me where your app lives (or open me in that repo) and I'll add it to the right view.
